description: First 50 seeds only - testing 'starting well' quality

scoring_criteria.9: Perfect native speech in both languages
scoring_criteria.1-2: Marginal, no one would say this

phrases.english: I would want to guess what you want to explain
phrases.other: Ik zou willen raden wat jij wil uit te leggen
phrases.qa_notes: English is awkward ('I would want to guess'). Dutch has incorrect infinitive construction - should be 'wilt uitleggen' not 'wil uit te leggen'. The 'te' before 'leggen' is wrong in this modal verb construction.

phrases.english: I like feeling as if I'm nearly ready to speak Dutch very well with everyone
phrases.other: Ik vind het fijn om te voelen alsof ik bijna klaar ben om heel goed Nederlands te spreken met iedereen
phrases.qa_notes: English is natural. Dutch is grammatically correct and natural, though quite long. Good word order with verb placement.

phrases.english: I started to think about it carefully last month about the sentence
phrases.other: Ik begon er vorige maand goed over na te denken wat de zin is
phrases.qa_notes: English is awkward - 'about the sentence' at the end is unnatural, redundant with 'about it'. Dutch has issues: 'nadenken over' is correct but the 'wat de zin is' clause doesn't fit naturally with the preceding structure.

phrases.english: I am not going to find out what the answer is soon because I don't want to learn
phrases.other: Ik ga binnenkort niet uitvinden wat het antwoord is omdat ik niet wil leren
phrases.qa_notes: English is functional but slightly awkward. Dutch word order is acceptable, though 'binnenkort niet' placement could be debated. 'Uitvinden' is correct for 'find out'.

phrases.english: I'm looking forward to remembering better what the sentence is tomorrow
phrases.other: Ik kijk ernaar uit om morgen beter te onthouden wat de zin is
phrases.qa_notes: English is slightly unnatural ('looking forward to remembering better'). Dutch is grammatically correct with proper separable verb 'uitkijken naar' and infinitive construction.

phrases.english: I'm trying to remember a word
phrases.other: Ik probeer een woord te onthouden
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are natural and correct. Simple, clear sentence with proper Dutch infinitive construction.

phrases.english: But you want to learn the whole name very well
phrases.other: Maar je wilt de hele naam heel goed leren
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are natural. Dutch word order is correct with verb 'leren' at the end. 'Heel goed' placement is natural.

phrases.english: I want to explain what I mean in Dutch
phrases.other: Ik wil in het Nederlands uit te leggen wat ik bedoel
phrases.qa_notes: English is fine. Dutch has a grammatical error: after 'willen' the infinitive should be 'uitleggen' NOT 'uit te leggen'. The 'te' is incorrect here - modal verb takes bare infinitive.

phrases.english: I wouldn't want to speak Dutch now
phrases.other: Ik zou niet willen nu Nederlands spreken
phrases.qa_notes: English is natural. Dutch word order is slightly off - 'nu' should typically come earlier: 'Ik zou nu niet willen Nederlands spreken' or better 'Ik zou nu geen Nederlands willen spreken'.

phrases.english: I want to speak something in Dutch
phrases.other: Ik wil iets in het Nederlands spreken
phrases.qa_notes: English is slightly awkward ('speak something'). Dutch is grammatically correct though 'iets in het Nederlands zeggen' might be more natural than 'spreken'.

phrases.english: I'm trying as hard as possible to remember a word
phrases.other: Ik probeer zo hard mogelijk een woord te onthouden
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are natural and correct. Good idiomatic expression in both languages.

phrases.english: I like feeling as if I'm nearly ready to meet people who speak Dutch this evening
phrases.other: Ik vind het fijn om te voelen alsof ik bijna klaar ben om vanavond mensen te ontmoeten die Nederlands spreken
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are natural and correct. Long but well-structured. Good use of relative clause 'die Nederlands spreken'.

phrases.english: I'm trying as hard as possible to speak Dutch today
phrases.other: Ik probeer vandaag zo hard mogelijk Nederlands te spreken
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are natural and correct. Good word order in Dutch with time adverb 'vandaag' placement.

phrases.english: I would like to try as hard as possible today
phrases.other: Ik zou graag vandaag zo hard mogelijk proberen
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are functional. Dutch is correct though slightly stilted. 'Zou graag willen' might be more natural but this is acceptable.

phrases.english: I want to practise
phrases.other: Ik wil oefenen
phrases.qa_notes: Perfect in both languages. Simple, natural, correct.

phrases.english: He wants to speak Dutch very well tomorrow
phrases.other: Hij wil morgen heel goed Nederlands spreken
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are natural and correct. Good Dutch word order.

phrases.english: I wouldn't like to speak Dutch after you are ready
phrases.other: Ik zou niet graag Nederlands spreken nadat jij klaar bent
phrases.qa_notes: English is slightly unnatural phrasing. Dutch is grammatically correct with proper subordinate clause verb order 'klaar bent'.

phrases.english: I like feeling as if I am nearly ready to speak Dutch very well with everyone
phrases.other: Ik vind het fijn om te voelen alsof ik bijna klaar ben heel goed Nederlands te spreken met iedereen
phrases.qa_notes: English is fine. Dutch is missing 'om' before 'heel goed Nederlands te spreken' - compare with idx 2 which has it correctly. Should be 'om heel goed Nederlands te spreken'.

phrases.english: She wants to speak in the Dutch language very well tomorrow
phrases.other: Zij wil morgen in het Nederlands heel goed spreken
phrases.qa_notes: English is slightly awkward ('in the Dutch language' is overly formal). Dutch is correct and natural.

phrases.english: It is useful to remember what the whole sentence is tomorrow morning
phrases.other: Het is nuttig morgen te onthouden wat de hele zin is
phrases.qa_notes: English is functional but awkward ('tomorrow morning' at end is odd). Dutch drops 'morgenochtend' (tomorrow morning) reducing to just 'morgen'. Missing 'om' before infinitive - should be 'om morgen te onthouden'.

phrases.english: easily remember
phrases.other: makkelijk onthouden
phrases.qa_notes: Fragment but both are natural. Dutch is correct.

phrases.english: And he would like to be able to speak later on after you are ready
phrases.other: En hij zou graag later kunnen spreken nadat jij klaar bent
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are acceptable. Dutch is grammatically correct with proper modal verb ordering and subordinate clause.

phrases.english: He wants to speak Dutch with everyone later on
phrases.other: Hij wil later met iedereen Nederlands spreken
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are natural and correct. Good word order in Dutch.

phrases.english: And she would like to explain what the answer is later on
phrases.other: En zij zou graag later willen uit te leggen wat het antwoord is
phrases.qa_notes: English is fine. Dutch has grammatical error: 'willen uitleggen' should be together, not 'willen uit te leggen'. The 'te' is incorrect after 'willen'.

phrases.english: I'm looking forward to not taking too much time to answer people
phrases.other: Ik kijk ernaar uit om niet te veel tijd te nemen om te antwoorden
phrases.qa_notes: English is somewhat awkward. Dutch drops 'people' and just has 'te antwoorden'. Structure is grammatically okay but slightly convoluted.

phrases.english: I don't like taking too much time to answer because I am not nearly ready
phrases.other: Ik vind het niet fijn om te veel tijd te nemen om te antwoorden omdat ik niet bijna klaar ben
phrases.qa_notes: English is functional. Dutch is grammatically correct but long. 'Niet bijna klaar' is a bit awkward - more natural would be 'nog lang niet klaar'.

phrases.english: I wanted yesterday
phrases.other: Ik wilde gisteren
phrases.qa_notes: Fragment - incomplete in both languages. Grammatically correct but lacks context/object.

phrases.english: She doesn't want to read anything about remembering what the answer is
phrases.other: Zij wil vanmiddag niets lezen onthouden wat het antwoord is
phrases.qa_notes: English is awkward ('read anything about remembering'). Dutch is broken - 'lezen onthouden' makes no sense, missing 'over' and proper construction. 'Vanmiddag' (this afternoon) appears in Dutch but not English.

phrases.english: We don't want to interrupt when someone wants to speak Dutch
phrases.other: Wij willen niet onderbreken als iemand Nederlands wil spreken
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are natural and correct. Good subordinate clause structure in Dutch.

phrases.english: I like to find out what the answer is tomorrow at six o'clock
phrases.other: Ik vind het fijn morgen om zes uur te uitvinden wat het antwoord is
phrases.qa_notes: English is fine. Dutch has error: 'te uitvinden' is wrong - should be 'uit te vinden' (separable verb). The particle 'uit' must separate from 'vinden' in infinitive with 'te'.

phrases.english: She wants to find out what I mean
phrases.other: Zij wil uitvinden wat ik bedoel
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are natural and correct. 'Uitvinden' is correct as bare infinitive after 'wil'.

phrases.english: I want to say the whole word in Dutch
phrases.other: Ik wil de hele woord in het Nederlands zeggen
phrases.qa_notes: English is fine. Dutch has gender error: 'woord' is neuter (het woord), so it should be 'het hele woord' not 'de hele woord'.

phrases.english: He doesn't want to meet people who speak Dutch very well this evening
phrases.other: Hij wil niet vanavond mensen ontmoeten die heel goed Nederlands spreken
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are acceptable. Dutch word order is slightly unusual with 'vanavond' placement but grammatically correct.

phrases.english: I want to learn something
phrases.other: Ik wil iets leren
phrases.qa_notes: Perfect in both languages. Simple, natural, correct.

phrases.english: I'm not sure if I can speak Dutch after I try
phrases.other: Ik weet niet zeker of ik Nederlands kan spreken nadat ik probeer
phrases.qa_notes: English is natural. Dutch is mostly correct but 'nadat ik probeer' is odd - should be 'nadat ik het probeer' or 'nadat ik geprobeerd heb' (after I've tried).

phrases.english: I like feeling as if I can remember what the answer is tomorrow
phrases.other: Ik vind het fijn om te voelen alsof ik morgen kan onthouden wat het antwoord is
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are natural and correct. Good structure with embedded clauses.

phrases.english: to speak something
phrases.other: iets spreken
phrases.qa_notes: Fragment. English 'to speak something' is slightly awkward (usually 'say something'). Dutch is correct as a phrase.

phrases.english: But she would like to find out what the answer is
phrases.other: Maar zij zou graag willen uitvinden wat het antwoord is
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are natural and correct. Good Dutch modal verb construction.

phrases.english: I don't like to take too much time to meet people who speak Dutch this evening
phrases.other: Ik vind het niet fijn om te veel tijd te nemen om vanavond mensen te ontmoeten die Nederlands spreken
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are functional and correct. Long but well-structured.

phrases.english: We don't want to start the story as quickly as possible
phrases.other: Wij willen niet zo snel mogelijk beginnen met het verhaal
phrases.qa_notes: English is functional. Dutch is correct with 'beginnen met' construction.

phrases.english: And we want to meet at six o'clock and find out what the answer is
phrases.other: En wij willen om zes uur afspreken en uitvinden wat het antwoord is
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are natural and correct. Good use of 'afspreken' for 'meet' in sense of making an appointment.

phrases.english: Did you want not to take too much time to answer people
phrases.other: Wilde je niet te veel tijd nemen om te antwoorden met mensen
phrases.qa_notes: English is awkward ('Did you want not to'). Dutch 'antwoorden met mensen' is wrong - should be 'aan mensen antwoorden' or 'mensen antwoorden'. 'Met' is incorrect preposition here.

phrases.english: how often you say something in Dutch
phrases.other: hoe vaak je iets in het Nederlands zegt
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are natural and correct. Good word order.

phrases.english: interrupt the story
phrases.other: het verhaal onderbreken
phrases.qa_notes: Fragment but both are natural and correct.

phrases.english: I would like that he wants to speak Dutch very often
phrases.other: Ik zou graag willen dat hij heel vaak Nederlands wil spreken
phrases.qa_notes: English is slightly awkward ('I would like that he wants'). Dutch is grammatically correct with proper 'dat' clause.

phrases.english: Are you going to help me speak Dutch very well before this evening
phrases.other: Ga je me helpen heel goed Nederlands te spreken voordat vanavond
phrases.qa_notes: English is acceptable. Dutch has a broken ending: 'voordat vanavond' is incomplete - needs a verb clause like 'voordat het vanavond is' or should be 'voor vanavond'.

phrases.english: I wanted yesterday to remember what the whole sentence is
phrases.other: Ik wilde gisteren onthouden wat de hele zin is
phrases.qa_notes: English word order is slightly awkward ('I wanted yesterday'). Dutch is correct.

phrases.english: I want to say the whole sentence in Dutch
phrases.other: Ik wil de hele zin in het Nederlands zeggen
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are natural and correct. Note: 'zin' is masculine so 'de hele zin' is correct (unlike idx 32 with 'woord').

phrases.english: I speak Dutch now to try to explain what I mean
phrases.other: Ik spreek nu Nederlands proberen uit te leggen wat ik bedoel
phrases.qa_notes: English is acceptable. Dutch is broken - missing 'om te' before 'proberen': should be 'Ik spreek nu Nederlands om te proberen uit te leggen wat ik bedoel'. As written, it's ungrammatical.

phrases.english: He doesn't want to be quiet when he wants to start talking as quickly as possible
phrases.other: Hij wil niet stil zijn als hij zo snel mogelijk wil beginnen met praten
phrases.qa_notes: Both languages are functional and correct. Good use of 'beginnen met praten'.

worst_3_phrases.english: She doesn't want to read anything about remembering what the answer is
worst_3_phrases.other: Zij wil vanmiddag niets lezen onthouden wat het antwoord is
worst_3_phrases.reason: Dutch is completely broken - 'lezen onthouden' is nonsensical, missing preposition 'over', and 'vanmiddag' appears in Dutch but not English. Translation mismatch and grammatical failure.

worst_3_phrases.english: I speak Dutch now to try to explain what I mean
worst_3_phrases.other: Ik spreek nu Nederlands proberen uit te leggen wat ik bedoel
worst_3_phrases.reason: Dutch missing required 'om te' construction before 'proberen'. The sentence is ungrammatical - infinitive clause requires 'om te proberen' to connect properly.

worst_3_phrases.english: I started to think about it carefully last month about the sentence
worst_3_phrases.other: Ik begon er vorige maand goed over na te denken wat de zin is
worst_3_phrases.reason: English has redundant 'about it...about the sentence'. Dutch structure is confused - 'nadenken over' is correct but the 'wat de zin is' clause doesn't integrate naturally.

common_issues: Incorrect infinitive constructions: 'uit te leggen' instead of 'uitleggen' after modal verbs (willen/kunnen)
Separable verb errors: 'te uitvinden' should be 'uit te vinden'
Missing 'om te' in infinitive purpose clauses
Article/gender errors: 'de hele woord' should be 'het hele woord'
Preposition errors: 'antwoorden met mensen' should be 'aan mensen antwoorden'
Incomplete subordinate clauses: 'voordat vanavond' is unfinished
English awkwardness in complex constructions that then compounds in Dutch translation
strengths: Basic word order is usually correct
Modal verb + infinitive basics are understood
Relative clauses ('die Nederlands spreken') are correct
Time adverb placement is generally acceptable
